title: A promote CI workflow runs on explicit manual trigger and accepts an optional versionId input
description: A CI workflow named `promote` (or the project's chosen equivalent) triggers only on manual operator action (`workflow_dispatch` on GitHub Actions or the equivalent explicit-trigger primitive on other CI platforms). It accepts one input field `versionId`: when supplied, the workflow promotes that exact version; when blank, the workflow calls the Deploy Adapter's `resolveNewestOfMain` verb to look up the current version id behind the preview alias and promotes THAT. It then invokes `promoteVersion` on the Deploy Adapter and, on success, invokes the served-surface verifier (REQ-010) before declaring the run successful. The workflow authenticates through the same named vendor CI secrets as `build-and-upload` and emits a structured record of the promote for the deploy log.
rationale: One workflow for both cases keeps the promote path narrow and reviewable. The empty-input default answers the common case (ship what merged); the explicit-id input answers hotfix promotes and rollbacks without a second code path. Every promote runs through the same served-surface verifier gate so no promote can quietly ship a broken version.
